title: FAA Part 107 remote pilot certificate and waivers practice questions
description: Free FAA Part 107 practice questions on the remote pilot certificate and waivers in 14 CFR 107. Every answer is explained and linked to its section.

questions.topic: Scope and who needs a certificate
questions.question: Under 107.12(c), whom may the Administrator, consistent with international standards, authorize to operate without an FAA-issued remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating?

options.A: Any person under 16 years of age flying for practice
options.B: Any person flying over a closed- or restricted-access site
options.C: An airman operating a civil foreign-registered small unmanned aircraft
options.D: Any visual observer who has watched ten flights

questions.explanation: 107.12(c): "The Administrator may, consistent with international standards, authorize an airman to operate a civil foreign-registered small unmanned aircraft without an FAA-issued remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.12, Requirement for a remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The Administrator may, consistent with international standards, authorize an airman to operate a civil foreign-registered small unmanned aircraft without an FAA-issued remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating.

questions.question: Which English language abilities does 107.61(b) require of an applicant for a remote pilot certificate?

options.A: Be able to read, speak, write, and understand the English language
options.B: Be able to read English only
options.C: Be able to speak English only
options.D: None, because no English language requirement applies

questions.explanation: 107.61(b): an applicant must "Be able to read, speak, write, and understand the English language."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.61, Eligibility (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Be able to read, speak, write, and understand the English language.

questions.question: Under 107.61(b), what may the FAA do if an applicant is unable to meet one of the English language requirements due to medical reasons?

options.A: Waive the aeronautical knowledge requirement
options.B: Require the applicant to hold a part 61 pilot certificate
options.C: Issue only a temporary certificate for 120 calendar days
options.D: Place such operating limitations on the applicant's certificate as are necessary for safe operation

questions.explanation: 107.61(b) says the FAA "may place such operating limitations on that applicant's certificate as are necessary for the safe operation of the small unmanned aircraft".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.61, Eligibility (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If the applicant is unable to meet one of these requirements due to medical reasons, the FAA may place such operating limitations on that applicant's certificate as are necessary for the safe operation of the small unmanned aircraft;

questions.question: Which physical or mental condition requirement does 107.61(c) set for an applicant?

options.A: Hold at least a third-class FAA medical certificate
options.B: Not know or have reason to know of a physical or mental condition that would interfere with the safe operation of a small UAS
options.C: Pass a medical examination every 24 calendar months
options.D: Submit a physician's statement with the application

questions.explanation: 107.61(c) requires that the applicant "Not know or have reason to know that he or she has a physical or mental condition that would interfere with the safe operation of a small unmanned aircraft system".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.61, Eligibility (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Not know or have reason to know that he or she has a physical or mental condition that would interfere with the safe operation of a small unmanned aircraft system;

questions.question: Under 107.61(d)(2), who may demonstrate aeronautical knowledge by completing training covering the areas of knowledge in 107.74?

options.A: Any holder of a student pilot certificate issued under part 61
options.B: A holder of a part 61 pilot certificate, other than a student pilot certificate, who meets the flight review requirements of 61.56
options.C: Any person who has flown small unmanned aircraft for recreation for at least 2 years
options.D: Any person who is at least 18 years of age

questions.explanation: 107.61(d)(2) applies "If a person holds a pilot certificate (other than a student pilot certificate) issued under part 61 of this chapter and meets the flight review requirements specified in § 61.56".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.61, Eligibility (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If a person holds a pilot certificate (other than a student pilot certificate) issued under part 61 of this chapter and meets the flight review requirements specified in § 61.56, complete training covering the areas of knowledge specified in § 107.74.

questions.question: Under 107.57(b), committing an act prohibited by which sections is grounds for denial of an application, or for suspension or revocation of a remote pilot certificate?
questions.explanation: 107.57(b): "Committing an act prohibited by § 91.17(a) or § 91.19(a) of this chapter is grounds for" denial of an application, or suspension or revocation of a remote pilot certificate.

questions.evidence: Committing an act prohibited by § 91.17(a) or § 91.19(a) of this chapter is grounds for:

questions.question: Which refusal does 107.59 make grounds for denial of an application or suspension or revocation of a remote pilot certificate?

options.A: A refusal to submit to a test to indicate the percentage by weight of alcohol in the blood when requested by a law enforcement officer in accordance with 91.17(c)
options.B: A refusal to let a visual observer assist with a flight
options.C: A refusal to complete recurrent training more often than every 24 calendar months
options.D: A refusal to register a small unmanned aircraft used only for recreation

questions.explanation: 107.59 covers "A refusal to submit to a test to indicate the percentage by weight of alcohol in the blood, when requested by a law enforcement officer in accordance with § 91.17(c) of this chapter".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.59, Refusal to submit to an alcohol test or to furnish test results (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A refusal to submit to a test to indicate the percentage by weight of alcohol in the blood, when requested by a law enforcement officer in accordance with § 91.17(c) of this chapter

questions.question: Under 107.63(a)(1), what must the evidence of passing the initial aeronautical knowledge test be when applying with a paper application?

options.A: A logbook endorsement from a certificated flight instructor
options.B: A certificate of completion of an online training course
options.C: An airman knowledge test report showing passage of the knowledge test
options.D: A signed statement from the applicant

questions.explanation: 107.63(a)(1): "If applying using a paper application, this evidence must be an airman knowledge test report showing passage of the knowledge test".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.63, Issuance of a remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If applying using a paper application, this evidence must be an airman knowledge test report showing passage of the knowledge test

questions.question: For an application under 107.63(a)(2), how does 107.63(b)(3) say the person making the application shows that the applicant meets the 61.56 flight review requirements?

options.A: By logbook endorsement or other manner acceptable to the Administrator
options.B: By an airman knowledge test report
options.C: By a copy of a current FAA medical certificate
options.D: By the small unmanned aircraft's registration certificate

questions.explanation: 107.63(b)(3) requires the person making the application to, "by logbook endorsement or other manner acceptable to the Administrator, show the applicant meets the flight review requirements specified in § 61.56".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.63, Issuance of a remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The person making the application must, by logbook endorsement or other manner acceptable to the Administrator, show the applicant meets the flight review requirements specified in § 61.56 of this chapter.

questions.question: Which event does 107.64(b) list as one upon which a temporary remote pilot certificate expires?

options.A: The holder's first flight at night
options.B: Renewal of the aircraft's Certificate of Aircraft Registration
options.C: A change in the holder's permanent mailing address
options.D: Receipt of the permanent certificate

questions.explanation: 107.64(b): a temporary certificate expires "On the expiration date shown on the certificate", "Upon receipt of the permanent certificate", or "Upon receipt of a notice that the certificate sought is denied or revoked."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.64, Temporary certificate (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A temporary remote pilot certificate with a small UAS rating expires: (1) On the expiration date shown on the certificate; (2) Upon receipt of the permanent certificate; or (3) Upon receipt of a notice that the certificate sought is denied or revoked.

questions.question: Which privileges does 107.65 say a person may not exercise unless the aeronautical knowledge recency requirement is met?

options.A: The privileges of registering a small unmanned aircraft
options.B: The privileges of acting as a visual observer
options.C: The privileges of a remote pilot in command with small UAS rating
options.D: The privileges of buying a small unmanned aircraft

questions.explanation: 107.65: "A person may not exercise the privileges of a remote pilot in command with small UAS rating unless that person has accomplished one of the following".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.65, Aeronautical knowledge recency (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A person may not exercise the privileges of a remote pilot in command with small UAS rating unless that person has accomplished one of the following in a manner acceptable to the Administrator within the previous 24 calendar months:

questions.question: Which of these does 107.65(b) list as a way to meet the aeronautical knowledge recency requirement?

options.A: Logging at least three flights in the previous 90 days
options.B: Completed recurrent training covering the areas of knowledge specified in 107.73
options.C: Renewing the small unmanned aircraft's registration
options.D: Completing a flight review under 61.56, with no small UAS training

questions.explanation: 107.65(b) lists "Completed recurrent training covering the areas of knowledge specified in § 107.73".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.65, Aeronautical knowledge recency (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Completed recurrent training covering the areas of knowledge specified in § 107.73; or

questions.question: Besides a photograph, signature and date of birth, what must an applicant's identification contain under 107.67(b)?

options.A: A Social Security number
options.B: An e-mail address
options.C: A small unmanned aircraft registration number
options.D: A permanent mailing address

questions.explanation: 107.67(b)(4) lists "Permanent mailing address"; if it is a post office box number, "the applicant must also provide a current residential address."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.67, Knowledge tests: General procedures and passing grades (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Permanent mailing address. If the applicant's permanent mailing address is a post office box number, then the applicant must also provide a current residential address.

questions.question: For what period does 107.69(b) prohibit an applicant found to have committed a prohibited act on a knowledge test from applying for any certificate, rating, or authorization and from taking any test?

options.A: 1 year after the date of committing that act
options.B: 14 calendar days after the date of committing that act
options.C: 24 calendar months after the date of committing that act
options.D: 6 months after the date of committing that act

questions.explanation: 107.69(b): such an applicant "is prohibited, for 1 year after the date of committing that act, from" applying for any certificate, rating, or authorization and applying for and taking any test.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.69, Knowledge tests: Cheating or other unauthorized conduct (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which area of knowledge is listed in 107.73 for the initial test and recurrent training but is not listed in 107.74 for qualifying part 61 pilots?

options.A: Operation at night
options.B: Crew resource management
options.C: Radio communication procedures
options.D: Emergency procedures

questions.explanation: 107.73(g) lists "Radio communication procedures"; the 107.74 list includes "Emergency procedures", "Crew resource management" and "Operation at night" but not radio communication procedures.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.73, Knowledge and training (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (g) Radio communication procedures;

questions.topic: Carrying the certificate, changes and surrender
questions.question: Under 107.77(a), what must accompany an application to change the name on a remote pilot certificate?

options.A: A new photograph and the applicant's knowledge test report
options.B: The remote pilot certificate with small UAS rating and a copy of the marriage license, court order, or other document verifying the name change
options.C: A new Certificate of Aircraft Registration
options.D: A letter from the applicant's employer

questions.explanation: 107.77(a): the application must be accompanied by the applicant's "Remote pilot certificate with small UAS rating" and "A copy of the marriage license, court order, or other document verifying the name change."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.77, Change of name or address (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: An application to change the name on a certificate issued under this subpart must be accompanied by the applicant's: (1) Remote pilot certificate with small UAS rating; and (2) A copy of the marriage license, court order, or other document verifying the name change.

questions.question: Under 107.7(b), what must the remote pilot in command, visual observer, owner, operator, or person manipulating the flight controls allow the Administrator to do upon request?

options.A: Fly the small unmanned aircraft on the operator's next job
options.B: Keep the small unmanned aircraft permanently
options.C: Review the operator's personal bank records
options.D: Make any test or inspection of the small unmanned aircraft system, the remote pilot in command, the person manipulating the flight controls, and, if applicable, the visual observer to determine compliance

questions.explanation: 107.7(b): they must, upon request, "allow the Administrator to make any test or inspection of the small unmanned aircraft system, the remote pilot in command, the person manipulating the flight controls of a small unmanned aircraft system, and, if applicable, the visual observer to determine compliance with this part."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.7, Inspection, testing, and demonstration of compliance (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The remote pilot in command, visual observer, owner, operator, or person manipulating the flight controls of a small unmanned aircraft system must, upon request, allow the Administrator to make any test or inspection of the small unmanned aircraft system, the remote pilot in command, the person manipulating the flight controls of a small unmanned aircraft system, and, if applicable, the visual observer to determine compliance with this part.

questions.question: Under 107.200(d)(1), to what extent may a person who receives a certificate of waiver deviate from the regulations of Part 107?

options.A: To the extent specified in the certificate of waiver
options.B: From any regulation of Part 107, without limit
options.C: Only from 107.51, whatever the waiver says
options.D: From any regulation for 24 hours after the waiver is issued

questions.explanation: 107.200(d)(1): a person who receives a certificate of waiver "May deviate from the regulations of this part to the extent specified in the certificate of waiver" and, under (d)(2), must comply with its conditions or limitations.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.200, Waiver policy and requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What limit does 107.205(a) place on waivers of 107.25, operation from a moving vehicle or aircraft?

options.A: No waiver will be issued for operations at night
options.B: No waiver will be issued for operations in Class B airspace
options.C: No waiver will be issued to allow the carriage of property of another by aircraft for compensation or hire
options.D: No waiver will be issued to a person under 18 years of age

questions.explanation: 107.205(a): "no waiver of this provision will be issued to allow the carriage of property of another by aircraft for compensation or hire."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.205, List of regulations subject to waiver (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 107.200(b), what must a request for a certificate of waiver contain?

options.A: Proof of liability insurance and the aircraft's registration certificate
options.B: A complete description of the proposed operation and justification that establishes that the operation can safely be conducted under the terms of a certificate of waiver
options.C: A declaration of compliance accepted under Subpart D
options.D: Written approval from local law enforcement

questions.explanation: 107.200(b): a request "must contain a complete description of the proposed operation and justification that establishes that the operation can safely be conducted under the terms of a certificate of waiver."
